title: Hairpin lace wall hanging
excerpt: A boho wall decor panel in chunky yarn using hairpin lace strips. Several strips hang side by side from a wooden dowel with their lower loops left open as fringe.
sourceNotes: Multiple hairpin lace strips mounted on a dowel, with alternate sides joined and lower loops left free to create a layered boho hanging.

glossaryTerms.definition: Attaching the top loops of a hairpin lace strip over a wooden dowel by slipping each loop onto the rod, then securing with slip stitches.
The lower loops of a hairpin strip left unworked so they hang freely, creating a fringed decorative edge.

crochet.gaugeText: Each strip = 8 cm wide with prongs set 8 cm apart.
crochet.finishedSizeText: Approx. 50 cm wide x 60 cm long (excluding fringe).

content.text: . The inner edges of adjacent strips are joined, while the lower edge loops are left as
Set the frame to 8 cm. Work each strip to 60 loops per side. Remove carefully and secure the live loops.

Using a slip stitch join, connect the right edge of strip 1 to the left edge of strip 2 along the top half of the loops only. Repeat for all five strips. Slide the top loops of each strip onto the dowel. Slip-stitch through each top loop to secure it to the rod.
Tie a length of yarn to each end of the dowel to hang the piece. Trim the lower fringe loops to an even length or leave them varied for a relaxed look. Weave in all ends with the tapestry needle.
